twopointsix · overnight, Aug 8

Animation pass: measure it, retime it, steady the head, give the body weight, plant the feet

The process the note asked about, as run tonight: a headless gait report (bun run tools/qa/gait.ts) drives the real character at fixed ground speeds and puts numbers on what stills hide — each loop’s natural ground speed, planted-foot slip, cadence, pelvis bob, eye-line pitch and bob, head yaw wobble, jerk, and now start / stop / turn transitions. Everything below was changed against those numbers first and eyeballed in filmstrips second.

The two big causes: the walk and crouch loops were being driven as if natural at 1.45 / 1.05 m/s when the planted toe says 1.06 / 0.72 (so every stride skated a third of its length), and nothing steadied the head, so the crouch and run clips stared at the floor and swung. Footstep loudness per step was rescaled with the retime so a guard hears the same over a stretch of floor.

Walk

Run

Standing: life, and feet that stay put

Also in the same layer: an acceleration-driven pelvis spring — from a walk he carries 4 cm on into a stop with a 2 cm dip and settles in 0.7 s, and tips into a start — so speed changes read as a body being moved rather than a cursor.

Not done, and what I’d like your eye on

  • The run is warped and lingered now (above) — every locomotion row slips ≤ 0.13 m/s; a calmer clip would still beat the deep knee at foot strike, which is authored into this one.
  • Walk cadence at 1.55 m/s is 2.2 steps/s — natural for the stride the clip has; a 10–15 % IK stride stretch would bring it to ~1.95 if it reads hurried to you.
  • Amplitudes to taste, all one-line constants in character.ts: breathing depth, weight-shift period (4–9 s) and travel (2.8 cm), the step-across trigger (26° / 11 cm) and arc (0.22 s, 4.5 cm), gaze targets per gait (4° / 9° / 12° below level), how much of the run’s bounce to keep (0.55).
  • The parked crouchSpeed question answered itself: the params are now the measured natural speeds and hearing was kept neutral per metre of floor.
